newsitem.title: INDIA: India to crack down on defaulting exporters.
newsitem.headline: India to crack down on defaulting exporters.

text.p: India is launching a campaign against businessmen who imported goods at concessional duty rates for export purposes but defaulted on their commitment to export, Commerce Secretary P.P. Prabhu said on Wednesday.
"We still have thousands of licensees who have not fulfilled their export obligations. The government has forgone about 20 million rupees in duty," Prabhu told a business conference.
"We are now going to start a drive against this. Where the obligations have not been fulfilled by exporters, it is necessary to implement the rules," he said.

Prabhu was responding to an appeal by the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) to extend the validity of advance licences for imports and the period for fulfilling export obligations.
"The point is that we should move away from a system where there is a need to approach the DGFT for a relaxation of policies," he said, referring to the Directorate-General of Foreign Trade.
In response to an appeal by FICCI to re-introduce a value-based advance licensing scheme for garment exporters, Prabhu said: "We would not like to multiply the number of schemes.
"But if we can accommodate various sectors within existing schemes, that is something we can consider," he added.
